reuse.why: The new finishLinkingAccount is used only by GoCardless and Fintegra; SimpleFin, PluggyAi, Akahu and EnableBanking keep their own upgrade-or-create/sync/notify copies, and the take-over reset copies unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount block instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Step 0's shared linking definition sits alongside four untouched copies of the same logic, the account-link reset is duplicated from unlinkAccount, and downloadFintegraTransactions copies the per-provider download template.

placement.why: Linking helpers are in accounts/app.ts where the link handlers live, but ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked mixes the closed-account rule and a mutation of another account under an 'ensure not linked' name, called from each wrapper rather than the shared path.

scope.why: Changes stay within linking, the Fintegra provider plumbing and their tests.

maintainability.why: A future change to linking still has to be made in five places (the shared function and four provider copies), defeating the stated purpose of step 0.

bypasses_abstraction.where: linkSimpleFinAccount, linkPluggyAiAccount, linkAkahuAccount and linkEnableBankingAccount in accounts/app.ts keep their own inline upgrade/create/sync code instead of calling finishLinkingAccount.

disguised_duplication.where: finishLinkingAccount is a reshaped (parameterised by source/create/tables) version of the four provider link bodies that remain in place, so the logic is copied into a new shape rather than shared.

abstraction_drift.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked takes a replaceExistingLink flag and has a closed-account branch and a take-over branch that clears another account; four of six link functions bypass finishLinkingAccount.
